name: Gong Mei

origin.regionNote: Fuding and Zhenghe; traditionally 菜茶 / small-leaf, not Da Bai

categoryNote: White tea is withered and dried. Withering is the process — there is no kill-green.
pluckStandard: bud and leaf from small-leaf bushes; not the Da Bai ladder

processing.description: Traditionally 菜茶 / 小白, not Fuding Da Bai. The market often files Gong Mei as a prettier name for Shou Mei; the older distinction is the bush.
The white-tea process: long wither, weather-dependent, no kill-green.
Sun and/or indoor dry. May be packed loose or pressed.

profile.mouthfeel: between Bai Mu Dan’s silk and Shou Mei’s rusticity

water.note: Medium-soft. Can take a little more heat than Yin Zhen.

storage: Dry and odour-free. Ages, but less often pressed than Shou Mei.

shelfLife.window: cakes breathe if ageing is the point
shelfLife.note: Sealed if drinking fresh, breathable if ageing. Both are legitimate and they are different intentions.

qualityMarkers.claim: small-leaf / 菜茶 named, not just “white tea grade 3”

commonFaults.name: Da Bai Shou Mei relabelled Gong Mei
commonFaults.tell: fat Da Bai buds and a Shou Mei price

compare.differentiator: Shou Mei is later Da Bai leaf. Gong Mei, in the older sense, is a different bush. Bags that use the names interchangeably are telling you the market, not the garden.

summary: The white-tea eyebrow that is supposed to be small-leaf 菜茶, sitting between White Peony and Shou Mei — when the name is honest.
